# bbox_annotation

**In one sentence:** The "Annotate Regions" modal. You draw boxes on each image, get a caption for each box from the captioning model, and send the whole batch back to the pipeline.

## Why it exists
The caption/bbox step (`prepare_lora_kit/steps/caption_bbox/workflow.py`) can ask a person to mark regions (bounding boxes, "bbox") on every image before captioning. This folder is that screen. It has one large canvas, a list of boxes beside it, and a filmstrip of all images below.

## What's inside
| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `bbox_annotation.js` | `showAnnotator(pending, { onSubmitted })` creates the `Annotator` class. It keeps one state per image, switches the canvas and panel when you pick another image, runs "Caption selected box", and handles Done, Skip image and Skip all remaining. |
| `batch.js` | Plain state helpers: `createImageStates` (from the payload), `effectiveSkipped`, `buildSubmitValue` (the `{ images: { path: { annotations, skipped } }, skip_all }` answer), `firstUncaptionedIndex`, and the strip badge / verdict classes. |
| `canvas.js` | `AnnotationCanvas` draws the image and boxes, and turns a mouse drag into a new box. Boxes smaller than 10px are ignored, and the label is asked for with `prompt()`. While dragging it listens on the window, because pywebview does not reliably keep pointer capture. |
| `canvas-render.js` | Drawing functions: `drawBox`, `dimOutsideBox` (darkens everything outside the selected box), `drawPendingRect`. |
| `canvas-utils.js` | Geometry helpers: pointer position to canvas pixels, `clampRect`, `normalizedFromPixels` (0–1 coords, 4 decimals), `fitCanvasSize`. |
| `box_panel.js` | `BoxPanel` is the side list. Each box gets a label input, a crop thumbnail, L/T/R/B pixel fields, and Select/Delete buttons. It also shows the status line. |
| `box-panel-utils.js` | Converts between 0–1 boxes and pixel edges, `attachShiftStep` (Shift+arrow or Shift+wheel moves 25px), `drawCropThumb`, `makeField`. |
| `thumbnail_strip.js` | `ThumbnailStrip` is the footer row of thumbnails. Each has a badge (done / has boxes / skipped / empty) and a tint when the caption verifier flagged it. |
| `bbox-annotation-utils.js` | `isUncaptioned(box)` (the label is blank or still the auto "region N") and `annotatorModal(count)`, which builds the modal markup. |
| `bbox_annotation.css` | Styles for the canvas area, box panel, coordinate fields and thumbnail strip. |

## How it works
- The job controller calls this for a pending interaction of kind `bbox_annotation`. `payload.images` has `path`, `uri`/`thumb_uri`/`view_uri`, saved `annotations`, `done` and `verdict`.
- Boxes are stored as 0–1 fractions of the image size. The canvas shows a smaller "view" image, and Python crops from the original image.
- "Caption selected box" calls `api().caption_region(jobId, path, box)`. While it runs, the whole modal is locked. The returned caption and crop info are saved on the box.
- If you edit an image, it is marked "dirty" and will be captioned again. An image that was done earlier and not touched is kept as it is.
- "Done" will not submit while any image that will be captioned still has an uncaptioned box. It jumps to that image and highlights the boxes.
- "Skip all remaining" keeps the current image and any edited images, and skips the rest.

## Who uses it
- `static/job/controller.js`: calls `showAnnotator` for `pending.kind === "bbox_annotation"`.
- `static/styles.css`: `@import`s `bbox_annotation.css`.
- Python side: `prepare_lora_kit_ui/runner/interactions.py` (`annotate_dataset`, `caption_region`) and `prepare_lora_kit_ui/bridge.py` (`caption_region`).
- Tests: `tests/ui/static/annotator.test.js`, `batch.test.js`, `canvas_render.test.js`.

## Good to know
- File names mix hyphens (`canvas-utils.js`, `box-panel-utils.js`, …) and underscores (`box_panel.js`, `thumbnail_strip.js`).
- `bbox-annotation-utils.js` holds two unrelated things: the caption check and the modal markup.
- `Annotator.nextIndex()` says it prefers "a later image still needing work". In fact it always returns the next index (or stays on the last image) without checking any state.
